questions: Are you experiencing involuntary shaking or trembling of your hands or arms?
Are the movements present when your hands are completely at rest?
Do they worsen when you hold your arms out or use your hands?
Do the movements decrease or stop when you are distracted?
Can you voluntarily stop the movements for a few seconds?
Do the movements change when you copy a rhythm with the other hand?
Is one side affected more than the other?
Do you have weakness in either arm or hand?
Do you have numbness, tingling, or loss of sensation?
Have you had problems with balance, walking, speech, or vision?
Have you had episodes of loss of awareness, fainting, or seizures?
Did this begin after an injury, illness, major stress, or upsetting event?
Have you recently started or changed any medications?
Do you use caffeine, stimulants, recreational drugs, or alcohol heavily?
Have you or a close relative ever had similar movements or a diagnosed neurological disorder?
served: surface EMG of forearm flexors and extensors
results: 1. limb power and wasting: mild distal finger muscle wasting
2. TSH / free T4: normal - not thyrotoxic
3. cervical spine MRI (including flexion views): ON NECK FLEXION, prominent flow voids in a widened posterior epidural space from C6 to T3 - diagnostic of Hirayama disease
4. nerve conduction studies / EMG: normal conduction velocity with NEUROGENIC changes in the C7-C8 myotome
5. surface EMG of forearm flexors and extensors: synchronous discharges at about 8 Hz in both forearm flexors and extensors
dx_raw:
DIAGNOSIS: Hirayama disease (flexion-induced cervical myelopathy/monomelic amyotrophy) with an action tremor caused by dynamic compression and ischemia of the lower cervical anterior horn cells, predominantly affecting the C7–C8 myotomes.

ALTERNATIVE: Essential tremor

ALTERNATIVE: Functional tremor

ALTERNATIVE: Tremor secondary to structural cervical cord disease other than Hirayama disease
